AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2, copied verbatim in substance. The sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation *is* construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from `__init__` (the_lost_and_forgotten.py:74-76). The game applies it from MonsterModel.AfterAddedToRoom awaited by CombatManager.AfterCreatureAdded inside StartCombatInternal, i.e. after every creature is on the board and before Hook.BeforeCombatStart; the sim runs it at create_monsters (combat.py:240-244), before relics attach (combat.py:272-274), before belt potions register (combat.py:279-281), before the parity Niche HP roll (combat.py:266-268) and before hooks.on_combat_start (combat.py:356). Same observable today on all three clauses: (a) listener set -- the four ported listeners on the reachable hooks (relics/ruined_helmet.py, relics/unsettling_lamp.py, relics/vambrace.py, relics/paels_legion.py) all gate on the player or on a non-null card and a monster's starting power is self-applied with no card; (b) HP-roll inversion -- of the 35 constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower mentions max_hp, and only inside revive() (powers.py:1581); (c) roll ordering -- EXECUTED, `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` prints `the_forgotten  sticky-no-op   initial=MIASMA (MoveState)`, so monster_state_machine step 30's early return fires and the constructor's first roll evaluates no branch and reads no power. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic, potion or power listening on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. Rule 7: the four relic files and powers.py are cited by name here and are NOT all hashed by this record. One C#-side detail worth naming: TheForgotten.cs:37-40 does NOT await base.AfterAddedToRoom() the way SoulNexus and LivingShield do. That is not a divergence for the sim to mirror -- MonsterModel.AfterAddedToRoom is `return Task.CompletedTask` (MonsterModel.cs:313-316), so calling it or not is identical. C# applies the power with `applier: null` (TheForgotten.cs:39); the sim passes no applier, which PossessSpeedPower's own record (audit/records/power/possess_speed.json) already verdicts faithful.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: TheForgotten.cs:42-51 is a pure two-cycle with NO branch state of any kind: MIASMA -> DREAD -> MIASMA, initial MIASMA. EXECUTED (`graphs`): the sim prints exactly `MIASMA -> DREAD` and `DREAD -> MIASMA`, initial=MIASMA. With no RandomBranchState, bug class 6 / monster_state_machine G1 cannot apply and no repeat rule or cooldown exists to be misread; the move sequence is deterministic on both sides and consumes no MonsterAi draw beyond the machine's own walk.

guards.what: MiasmaMove's three sub-effects and their ORDER -- load-bearing, because the block is gained BEFORE the Dexterity that would raise it
guards.rationale: TheForgotten.cs:53-60: Apply<DexterityPower>(targets, -2) -> GainBlock(Creature, 8m, ValueProp.Move) -> Apply<DexterityPower>(Creature, +2). the_lost_and_forgotten.py:95-101 is the identical three in the identical order (player -2 Dex with applier=self, BlockCmd 8 with ValueProp.MOVE, self +2 Dex). The order is observable and not cosmetic: because the self-buff comes LAST, the block on the Nth Miasma is 8 + 2*(N-1), not 8 + 2*N. Both sides route the block through the powered-block modifier chain (ValueProp.Move / ValueProp.MOVE), so the monster's own Dexterity does apply to it. DebilitatingSmogDexStealAmount is GetValueIfAscension(DeadlyEnemies, 2, 2) = 2 on both branches, and the block literal is 8m.

guards.what: DreadDamage reads the monster's own Dexterity at telegraph time
guards.rationale: TheForgotten.cs:24-31 `GetValueIfAscension(DeadlyEnemies, 15, 13) + Creature.GetPowerAmount<DexterityPower>()` = 13 + own Dex -- an unusual use of Dexterity as ATTACK scaling, and it is deliberate (the monster attacks with the speed it drains). It is wrapped in a lambda at the intent site (`new SingleAttackIntent(() => DreadDamage)`, TheForgotten.cs:46) so the telegraph tracks the current Dexterity. the_lost_and_forgotten.py:78-80 (`_dread_damage` = 13 + dex.amount, 0 when absent) and the `lambda: Intent(...)` at :89 reproduce both halves, and _dread (:103-104) recomputes the same value at perform time exactly as DreadMove does (TheForgotten.cs:64).

monsters/base.py `_execute_attack` fires before_attack, loops `hits` times through DamageCmd.deal and breaks when the player or the attacker is dead; then after_attack. C#'s AttackCommand.Execute (AttackCommand.cs:528-546) has the same two loop guards -- `if (Attacker.IsDead) break;` and an empty alive-target list -- and the sim's single target IS the player, so the two loops agree hit for hit. The one asymmetry is C#'s PRE-loop `if (Attacker.IsDead) return this;` (AttackCommand.cs:528-531), which also skips Hook.BeforeAttack; the sim has no such pre-guard. Unreachable for this unit and EXECUTED rather than asserted (rule 5): a sim monster can only take a turn while dead if `retained_after_death` is set (combat.py, :306), that flag is written only where hooks.should_remove_from_combat_after_death returns False (cmds.py, :200-202), and `grep -rn 'def should_remove_from_combat_after_death' sts2_rl/` returns exactly two sites -- the hook itself (hooks.py) and ReattachPower (powers.py:2338), which this monster never holds.

TheLostAndForgottenNormal.cs generates (TheLost, null) then (TheForgotten, null), RoomType.Monster; THE_LOST_AND_FORGOTTEN_NORMAL (the_lost_and_forgotten.py:107-110) is `[TheLost, TheForgotten]` in the same order, which fixes the enemy slot order and therefore the CombatId numbering the replay targets by.
